items.title: Tolliver interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: Because Art Blakey’s well-said powerful in that inimitable voice of his, you know, when he would get off the drums and speak to the audience and said, “We’re here to wash away the dust of your everyday life.”

ctx.x: Well it makes me wonder, I was sort of going to ask this question wherever our interview wraps up, but I’ll try it now. Do you feel that you have sacrificed or given anything up for this music?

Absolutely not. If I had it to do all over again I’d do exactly the same. Every bit of it you know. I mean we are blessed in a way, you know, us artisans I mean and it doesn’t matter which idiom it is: jazz music, classical music, popular music, minimalist, you know. Because Art Blakey’s well-said powerful in that inimitable voice of his, you know, when he would get off the drums and speak to the audience and said, “We’re here to wash away the dust of your everyday life.” And so I carry that in mind you know. And…
When you recorded, performed and composed, did you have something in mind that you hoped your audience would glean from your work?
